intro_script: Welcome to your daily research digest from October 23, 2026. We've got ten fascinating updates today, including breakthroughs in ML agents, LLM efficiency, and automated behavior elicitation.

items.title: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
items.summary: Frontier coding agents are tested on the demanding task of improving published scientific models, which requires domain insight beyond standard ML engineering. Agent4Sci is introduced as a long-horizon testbed to measure the extent to which these agents can advance scientific ML benchmarks in real-world conditions. Empirically, agents achieved relative improvements by using engineering tricks rather than deep research insight. Trajectory analysis revealed limitations such as novelty miscalibration, resource under-utilization, and rapid regression to local engineering sweeps. The work proposes lightweight plug-in skills to bridge the gap between ML engineering and domain insight for these agents.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?". This story details the testing of frontier coding agents on improving published scientific models, revealing that agents achieved relative improvements primarily through engineering tricks rather than deep research insight. Agent4Sci was introduced as a long-horizon testbed designed to measure the advancement of these agents in scientific machine learning benchmarks under real-world conditions. Trajectory analysis uncovered limitations including novelty miscalibration, resource under-utilization, and a rapid regression to local engineering sweeps during the process. The research proposes the use of lightweight plug-in skills to connect machine learning engineering with necessary domain insight for these agents. This research indicates a gap between pure engineering and necessary scientific understanding in current AI applications. Further development is required to bridge this gap effectively.

items.title: MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
items.summary: MoEZip is a method for routing-aware KV cache compression specifically for sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models. It addresses the issue that standard compression methods neglect how KV cache eviction affects expert routing, which can degrade generation quality. The method introduces a novel metric based on the Fisher information matrix of routing distributions combined with attention weights for context scoring. MoEZip integrates complementary scoring systems to handle both dense and sparse MoE architectures effectively. Experiments demonstrate that MoEZip significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art by improving scores on LongBench and RULER benchmarks under aggressive cache compression.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs" describes a method for routing-aware KV cache compression specifically for sparse Mixture-of-Experts language models, showing significant performance improvements on benchmark tests. The method introduces a novel metric based on the Fisher information matrix of routing distributions combined with attention weights for context scoring to address the limitation of standard compression methods neglecting expert routing effects. MoEZip integrates complementary scoring systems to manage both dense and sparse MoE architectures, demonstrating that this approach significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques when cache compression is applied across LongBench and RULER benchmarks. This development indicates a pathway for more effective and quality-preserving memory management in large sparse language models.

items.title: Fig: Automated Multiagent Behavior Elicitor
items.summary: An agentic system named Fig automates the elicitation of behaviors in multiagent systems by performing targeted interventions on game environments. It takes natural language behavior descriptions, decomposes them, and generates interventions to influence agents, opponents, or context. Evaluation combines mechanical checks and synthetic rubric judgments, validated through human review. Fig successfully elicited target behaviors, achieving an average attempt rate of 45.2% across six behaviors. The system demonstrates that multiagent environments are effective programmable testbeds for controllable behavior evaluation.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Fig: Automated Multiagent Behavior Elicitor" details an agentic system designed to automate the elicitation of behaviors within multiagent systems through targeted interventions in game environments, achieving an average attempt rate of forty-five point two percent across six behaviors. The system functions by taking natural language descriptions of desired behaviors, decomposing them, and generating specific interventions intended to influence agents, opponents, or the surrounding context. The evaluation process combines mechanical checks with synthetic rubric judgments, which are subsequently validated through human review. This methodology demonstrates that multiagent environments serve as effective programmable testbeds for the controllable evaluation of agent behavior. The findings suggest a pathway for systematically testing and verifying complex behaviors in artificial intelligence systems.

items.title: Decision language models as affordable and rapid alternatives to LLM judges of clinical generative AI
items.summary: Decision language models (like Jev) offer an affordable and rapid alternative to using large language model judges for clinical generative AI. Comparisons showed Jev's agreement with physician quality ratings matched or exceeded that of several LLM judges across various clinical evaluations. Frontier LLM judges were significantly more costly and slower than Jev. This suggests that decision language models can enable efficient clinical AI evaluation at scale. Ultimately, Jev demonstrates potential for streamlining the assessment of clinical generative AI.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Decision language models as affordable and rapid alternatives to LLM judges of clinical generative AI" reports on the use of decision language models as a more cost-effective and faster alternative to employing large language model judges for evaluating clinical generative artificial intelligence. Comparisons demonstrated that decision language models achieved agreement with physician quality ratings that matched or surpassed that of several large language model judges across various clinical evaluations. Frontier large language model judges were found to be significantly more costly and slower than the decision language models presented. This indicates that decision language models possess the capacity to facilitate efficient clinical artificial intelligence assessment at scale. The development suggests a pathway for streamlining the evaluation process of clinical generative AI.

items.title: Automated screening of privacy risks in medical AI
items.summary: Medical AI models risk privacy breaches through membership inference attacks, even when training data is not shared. A significant issue is that risks are often reported as cohort averages, masking individual patient exposure. The research measured patient vulnerability across numerous models and datasets to identify potentially exposed records. A lightweight screening tool using four small models was developed to identify high-risk patients before production model training. This screening process suggests privacy assessment should be integrated into the data preparation phase for clinical AI.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "Automated screening of privacy risks in medical AI" reports on the privacy risks associated with medical artificial intelligence models through membership inference attacks, even without sharing the training data. The research measured patient vulnerability across numerous models and datasets to identify potentially exposed records. A lightweight screening tool employing four small models was developed to identify high-risk patients prior to production model training, suggesting that privacy assessment should be integrated into the data preparation phase for clinical artificial intelligence. This automated screening process offers a method for mitigating privacy exposure in medical AI systems. The industry should prioritize integrating privacy risk assessment directly into the data preparation pipeline for clinical AI development.

items.title: High-Value Training Data from Noisy, Diverse Sources
items.summary: Training state-of-the-art models from large, diverse, and noisy datasets requires effectively managing the influence of various training examples. A scalable method is developed to learn dataweights by using metagradients from a small, high-quality target dataset. This approach allows for the learning of parametric weighting rules that generalize to new, streaming data and scale across different model sizes. Reward modeling serves as a key application, demonstrating that learned dataweights improve performance and allow for effective mixing of human and synthetic supervision. Ultimately, these learned weights enhance performance and adapt reward models to specialized domains despite noisy supervision.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "High-Value Training Data from Noisy, Diverse Sources" reports on a scalable method for training state-of-the-art models from large, diverse, and noisy datasets by learning dataweights using metagradients from a small, high-quality target dataset. The methodology involves learning parametric weighting rules that generalize to new, streaming data and scale across different model sizes. Reward modeling is presented as a key application, demonstrating that these learned dataweights improve performance and enable effective mixing of human and synthetic supervision. This approach allows learned weights to enhance performance and adapt reward models to specialized domains despite noisy supervision. This development points toward more robust and adaptable methods for training artificial intelligence systems with real-world, imperfect data.

items.title: A Small Model Asks Better: Fine-Tuning Query Clarification for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: Query clarification is necessary in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems when user queries are ambiguous or contextually unclear. The study addresses scenarios where queries are ill-formed or have multiple relevant interpretations based on retrieved documents. A new dataset, ClariEdge, containing ambiguous and non-ambiguous queries is introduced for this task. A lightweight fine-tuned LoRA model achieves high classification accuracy, outperforming larger models in clarifying query quality. Hard negative examples are shown to be crucial for distinguishing truly ambiguous queries from those that are merely contextually complex.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "A Small Model Asks Better: Fine-Tuning Query Clarification for Retrieval-Augmented Generation" details a method for improving query clarification within Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems. The research introduced a new dataset called ClariEdge to address scenarios where user queries are ambiguous or lack contextual clarity based on retrieved documents. A lightweight fine-tuned LoRA model was developed to perform this query clarification task, demonstrating high classification accuracy and outperforming larger models in assessing query quality. The study utilized hard negative examples, which were shown to be essential for accurately distinguishing genuinely ambiguous queries from those that are simply contextually complex. This research indicates a method for enhancing the reliability of information retrieval processes in generative AI applications.

items.title: Forging More Tasks into Better Harnesses: Agentic Harness Evolution via Successive Scale Racing
items.summary: Agentic harness evolution uses task execution experiences to optimize an agent's instructions and tools. A failure mode emerges where expanding the task pool causes existing methods to degrade due to suboptimal evidence selection. Successive Scale Racing (SSR) is proposed to address this by adaptively searching for optimal evidence combinations in each evolution round. SSR races candidate harnesses based on task quality and coverage within a limited compute budget. Empirically, SSR achieved state-of-the-art results across benchmarks while improving performance as the task pool increased.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Forging More Tasks into Better Harnesses: Agentic Harness Evolution via Successive Scale Racing" details a method for optimizing agentic harness evolution through successive scale racing. The research introduces Successive Scale Racing to counteract performance degradation when expanding task pools in agentic harness evolution by adaptively searching for optimal evidence combinations in each evolution round. The method races candidate harnesses based on task quality and coverage within a defined compute budget, demonstrating the ability to achieve state-of-the-art results across benchmarks while showing performance improvement as the task pool increases. This work suggests a scalable approach for improving agent capabilities by iteratively refining the interaction between tasks and the tools an agent utilizes. Further investigation into the efficiency of this scaling process is warranted within the artificial intelligence field.

items.title: Sketch2Sim: an end-to-end modular framework for hand-drawn circuit analysis
items.summary: Sketch2Sim is an end-to-end modular framework designed to analyze hand-drawn circuit diagrams. It converts raw sketches into SPICE-compatible netlists and automatically calculates nodal voltages and currents. The system employs a multi-stage pipeline involving YOLO detectors, a CRNN for symbol extraction, and image processing for node identification. A dataset of 1,000 RLC circuits was used to train the system, demonstrating robust performance across different handwriting styles. This framework aims to enhance education and expedite engineering design reviews.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Sketch2Sim: an end-to-end modular framework for hand-drawn circuit analysis" details an end-to-end modular framework designed to analyze hand-drawn circuit diagrams and convert them into SPICE-compatible netlists while calculating nodal voltages and currents. The system employs a multi-stage pipeline involving YOLO detectors, a CRNN for symbol extraction, and image processing for node identification. Training utilized a dataset of one thousand RLC circuits, demonstrating robust performance across varied handwriting styles. This framework aims to enhance education and expedite engineering design reviews by automating the analysis of complex diagrams. This development indicates progress in applying deep learning to automate the interpretation of manual technical drawings.

items.title: Benchmarking Model Compression Techniques Across Heterogeneous Edge Platforms: A Predictive Maintenance Use Case for Rotating Machinery
items.summary: The paper compares four model compression techniques on a convolutional neural network for predictive maintenance across nine heterogeneous edge platforms. The evaluation focused on classification performance, inference speed, and compression ratio using real-world rotating machinery data. Knowledge distillation was identified as the most effective compression method, achieving over a 90% speedup while maintaining a 91.22% balanced F-score. This approach resulted in a 98.9% size reduction of the model. The study demonstrates a method to reduce computational costs in industrial settings for achieving Industry 5.0 goals.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "Benchmarking Model Compression Techniques Across Heterogeneous Edge Platforms: A Predictive Maintenance Use Case for Rotating Machinery" details a comparison of model compression methods on heterogeneous edge platforms for a predictive maintenance application. The study found that knowledge distillation proved to be the most effective compression technique, yielding an inference speedup exceeding ninety percent while sustaining a ninety-one point two two percent balanced F-score. This method achieved a ninety-eight point nine percent reduction in model size when applied to a convolutional neural network analyzing rotating machinery data across nine different edge systems. This research presents a viable method for reducing computational costs in industrial environments to support Industry 5.0 objectives. The findings indicate a path toward deploying more efficient and practical artificial intelligence solutions in industrial settings.

items.title: GANet: A Lightweight Group Attention Network for Plant Disease Identification on Embedded Systems
items.summary: GANet is a lightweight Group Attention Network developed for identifying plant diseases on embedded systems. It utilizes novel Group Attention and Group-Wise Feature Fusion blocks to achieve sparsity and efficiency. The model requires only 0.001M parameters and achieves 99.99% accuracy on the PlantVillage dataset. GANet is optimized for deployment on edge devices like Raspberry Pi 4b and Jetson Nano. This allows for real-time plant disease monitoring with speeds of 5 FPS and 11 FPS respectively.

items.title: Edit, Don't Imitate: Minimal-Edit On-Policy Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning
items.summary: Visual mathematical reasoning can suffer from errors when a vision-language model misreads diagrams, creating false premises for reasoning. The proposed method uses minimal-edit on-policy distillation to correct these errors using reference descriptions and solutions as training information. A teacher scores incorrect student outputs based on a minimal-edit objective, focusing loss only on teacher-disfavored tokens. Correct rollouts are reinforced with task-reward reinforcement learning, preserving on-policy supervision without full imitation. This technique improves perception-oriented performance and transfers to external mathematics benchmarks.

items.title: Differentially Private Synthetic Data via Generalized Moment Matching
items.summary: The research introduces a method for generating differentially private synthetic data for databases in the $[-1,1]^d$ space under an integral probability metric. Generalized moment matching is utilized to privately estimate moments, fit a probability measure, and sample synthetic records. A general error theorem connects moment error to the target IPM, extending Chebyshev moment matching for 1-Wasserstein distance. The framework applies to objectives like maximum mean discrepancy and provides guarantees for sliced Wasserstein-1 distances. These methods yield minimax optimal rates for fixed dimensions when sufficient synthetic data is available.

items.title: Prediction Uncertainty Controlled Computer Model Calibration
items.summary: A two-layer framework is proposed to control prediction uncertainty in computer model calibration. The first layer uses a conditional flow-matching model to learn an amortized posterior for calibration parameters based on perturbed simulator outputs. The second layer employs conformal risk control to arrange posterior draws into nested sets, selecting the smallest set whose pointwise bands achieve a target miscoverage. This method controls expected miscoverage in finite samples, showing sharper bands than prior methods for a benchmark. Application to an age-structured SEIR model demonstrated that the resulting uncertainty bands exposed structural model inadequacies.

items.title: AI Mindmeld: A Latent Interconnect Protocol
items.summary: Large Language Models can be augmented by direct representation exchange, referred to as the Latent Interconnect Protocol (LIP). LIP learns connectors that map specialist representations into the LLM's internal states, enabling information exchange without joint training. The protocol successfully connected protein and small molecule specialists to Gemma 3 and Kimi K2.6 models. Independently trained connectors allow for zero-shot transfer to cross-domain tasks. The work suggests specialist developers and LLM developers must collaborate to establish consistent representation interfaces for scientific agents.

items.title: SpecEvo: Speculative Evolution with Large Language Models for Cost-Efficient Scientific Discovery
items.summary: SpecEvo is a multi-LLM framework designed for cost-efficient scientific discovery by coordinating lightweight and frontier models. It uses lightweight models for parallel speculation and evidence consolidation, while frontier models intervene strategically at sparse checkpoints. This workflow delegates routine exploration to inexpensive models, reserving high-level reasoning for crucial interventions. Results show SpecEvo outperforms baselines while reducing API costs by up to 80% across various discovery tasks. The method demonstrates effective trajectory-conditioned model coordination for efficient scientific exploration.

items.title: To Manipulate or Not: Opinion Dynamics in LLM Interactions
items.summary: The research introduces a controlled LLM-LLM debate framework to study opinion dynamics in extended conversations. Two language models, GPT-6 Luna and Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite, are used to discuss climate-change attribution, with one model assigned a stance and the other not. Opinion dynamics varied based on model combinations, as same-model interactions narrowed the opinion gap while cross-model interactions widened it. Explicit reports and in-dialogue behavior reveal different aspects of this dynamic, and a simple persuasion instruction was not consistently effective. These findings indicate that conversational influence depends on the participating models, not just assigned roles and initial positions.

items.title: Speedrunning Relational Foundation Model Pretraining
items.summary: Relational foundation model pretraining is decentralized through speedrunning leaderboards to overcome barriers in accessing private training recipes. The work introduces modded-nanoRT, a leaderboard for Relational Transformers, which fixes the benchmark by calibrating the selection based on learning curve separation. The method utilizes a relational operator, typed trilinear attention, along with Muon and SIGReg. The resulting recipe achieves a target in 305.63 seconds on one GPU, significantly faster than the reference. The authors plan to release the benchmark, frozen artifacts, and record runs for public use.

items.title: Prediction Is Not Calibration: Item Parameter Recovery and Representation Coupling in Knowledge Tracing
items.summary: Predictive accuracy in knowledge tracing models does not guarantee the recovery of item parameters. The study investigates item parameter recovery and representation coupling using various item response decoders and encoders. Findings indicate that while difficulty and mean threshold recovery is robust, discrimination and option slope recovery depend heavily on the scale and spread of estimated ability. Separating the sequence representation from the item parameter key improves recovery and cross-order consistency without sacrificing test accuracy. Ultimately, item parameters like discrimination must be evaluated separately from response prediction.

items.title: When Reconstruction Is Not Enough: Doubly Robust Counterfactual and Interventional Mediation Analysis with Learned Multimodal Representations
items.summary: Learned multimodal representations for health records are often trained for reconstruction, which may not suffice for causal identification. The study examines counterfactual outcomes and interventional effects under exposure-induced confounding using these representations. It demonstrates that interventional mediation is more demanding than counterfactual comparison in this context. No training objective, including reconstruction, can guarantee a representation's sufficiency, as insufficient representations can lead to large bias despite low reconstruction error. A workflow combining specific methods is proposed to address representation insufficiency and provide diagnostic checks.

items.title: Metric Conformal Prediction via the Conditional Expected Local Radius
items.summary: The method introduces the conditional expected local radius (CELR) to facilitate metric conformal prediction in general metric spaces. CELR quantifies local conditional probability concentration, enabling prediction sets that handle heterogeneity without requiring density or vector space structures. A novel conformal prediction method is developed using this measure, which yields a nonconformity score comparable across covariate values. The approach adapts a metric distributional random forest to manage multivariate covariates and nonlinear interactions efficiently. Numerical studies confirm the method's effectiveness in uncertainty quantification and computational savings compared to other scoring methods.

items.title: Flow-based Spectral Kernel Learning for Nonstationary Attention
items.summary: Flow-based spectral kernel attention (FSKA) is proposed as a framework for learning expressive, nonstationary attention kernels. It achieves this by formulating kernelized attention through spectral density learning and parameterizing the spectral density using normalizing flows. This design allows for flexible and regularizable kernel learning compatible with scalable linear-attention computation. FSKA simplifies attention design by removing query-key and fixed orthogonal value projections, leading to a more parameter-efficient architecture. Experimental results show FSKA achieves competitive or improved performance while reducing trainable parameters by $40\%$--$47\%$.

items.title: Deep Learning for Random Objects in Metric Spaces: Beyond Manifold Assumptions
items.summary: Deep learning methods are proposed for regression involving random objects in metric spaces, moving beyond traditional manifold or Euclidean embedding assumptions. The framework operates directly on the metric structure of the response space, while maintaining statistical guarantees. Statistical consistency and convergence rates are established for the proposed estimator, showing its potential to mitigate the curse of dimensionality. Simulation studies confirm competitive predictive performance across various configurations. Practical utility was demonstrated in digital health case studies using Wasserstein spaces with real-world data.

items.title: xVGAE: A Hierarchical Variational Graph Autoencoder for Exchangeable Graphs
items.summary: The xVGAE is a Hierarchical Variational Graph Autoencoder designed for exchangeable graphs. It is inspired by the Aldous-Hoover theorem, which characterizes graph distributions invariant to node permutations. The model learns an approximation of graphons and latent variables from a training set of graphs. xVGAE can generate new graphs quickly that closely match the statistics of the training data. This approach enables fast and high-quality graph generation for applications where standard models face computational limitations.

items.title: Why Constrained Updates Still Forget: A Functional-Path Analysis of Continual SFT
items.summary: Supervised fine-tuning can disrupt previously acquired behavior, and existing constraints do not clearly explain the relationship between protected objects, trajectories, and retained outputs. The research introduces a functional-path account to decompose old-loss changes during updates into controlled directions, gradient staleness, probe mismatch, and finite-step effects. This account identifies a conditional refresh budget and the restoring direction provided by informative replay. Different constraint placements and granularities impact retention differently across code-label audits and checkpointed generation. The findings suggest mitigating forgetting requires explicit functional anchors and joint auditing of old and new data.

items.title: Random Projections for Spectral Algorithms: Optimal Rates in Sobolev Norms
items.summary: Random projections effectively reduce computational overhead in spectral algorithms while preserving data structure. The paper establishes optimal learning rates in Sobolev norms for these Random Projection (RP)-based methods under general conditions. Using RKHS embedding and operator similarity analysis, the authors find the required projection dimension is proportional to the effective dimension. This optimality holds across a wide range of source conditions without relying on uniform boundedness assumptions. Experimental results confirm the theoretical validity and practical effectiveness of these projection methods.

items.title: How Prompt Style Affects AI Accuracy and Speed in Competitive Programming
items.summary: Exploratory study of prompt styles on GPT-5.5 across tasks from the International Olympiad in Informatics and NP-hard speed tasks was conducted. No single prompt style was found to be optimal, as the best style depended on the specific task and result summarization method. Differences in accuracy stemmed from outlier runs, indicating that single metrics can obscure the true effect of prompting. Comparing results to human contestants showed the AI was neither strictly better nor worse than humans across all tasks. Extending the comparison to runtime speed and human performance provides a more comprehensive view of prompt style's impact.

items.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
items.summary: Continued pre-training across data volume, diversity, and model size was investigated for embodied agents in diverse virtual worlds. Results indicated that more data improves in-corpus performance, diversity helps transfer to related worlds, and model size affects data efficiency and generalization to distant worlds. An early interface phase followed by a later world phase was observed, aligning with an empirical scaling law for validation loss. Models proved competitive in 3D settings, yet limitations in imitation suggest further training stages are necessary for generalist agents.

items.title: Spectral Uncertainty Decomposition for Sparse Bayesian Learning
items.summary: Estimating neural sources from M/EEG measurements is an ill-posed inverse problem where uncertainty quantification is challenging. The proposed spectral framework uses the singular value structure of the prior-preconditioned forward operator to decompose the posterior covariance. This decomposition separates uncertainty into data-informed and fundamentally irreducible epistemic components. A subtractive decomposition is also derived, expressing the prior covariance as a sum of posterior and data-driven reduction terms. These methods provide interpretable uncertainty quantification for linear-Gaussian Bayesian inverse solvers in M/EEG source imaging.

items.title: Continuous-depth Deep Gaussian Processes
items.summary: Deep Gaussian Processes are proposed with a continuous-depth formulation to address optimization difficulties in discrete-depth models. This formulation treats depth as a continuous evolution governed by a stochastic differential equation with a GP-based prior on the drift family. Two instantiations are studied: CDGP, which has a direct GP prior over the state-depth drift, and FlowDGP, which uses a flow-evolved prior for richer depth dependence. The research analyzes the sensitivity of the single-sample DGP objective and evaluates performance on various regression tasks. Experiments indicate that residual DGP improves upon plain DGP, while CDGP and FlowDGP offer superior results.
